entries.title: Plan: a portfolio of specialists, picked per kingdom
entries.html:
Steam deals 10 of the 26 cards at random, and a GA genome trained on one fixed kingdom only knows those 10. The new model is a portfolio: about twenty specialists, each evolved with all 26 cards on fresh random kingdoms that always hold its key cards (Witch, Militia, Smithy, Laboratory, Library, Gardens + Workshop, Village + Smithy…), plus a generalist for any kingdom.

The picker is a model too, but not a learned one: when a game starts it plays every specialist on that exact kingdom against the benchmark bots on the C engine (about 25,000 games per second) and the best one plays the game. The new trainer is ga/specialist.py, the model kind ga-portfolio (policy/portfolio.py), and the model goes in its own folder, models/portfolio-v1/.

The nine cards the autopilot can't play on Steam yet (Cellar, Remodel, Library…) are in training. During play they are never bought, and the picker tries each specialist the same way, so it picks one that wins without them. One run, generalist-safe, trains without them as a fallback.

entries.title: A benchmark bug, fixed: every kingdom now gets its own games
entries.html:
The first Witch specialist stalled at the same validation score many times, and the per-bot numbers were suspiciously round (95.0%, 62.5%). The cause: every kingdom in a test set reused the same game seeds. When neither player buys the other kingdom cards, a Witch-and-money deck plays exactly the same game on all 60 kingdoms, so “60 kingdoms × 10 seeds” was really 10 games per seat. The model benchmark (policy.bench) had the same flaw.

Fixed in both: each kingdom gets its own seeds (benchmark version 3), and all models were re-measured. The best old model, k4-20260614, scores 78.9% (it was 81.5%), and k1-steam, the model behind every Steam game so far, scores 43.7%. Those are the numbers to beat. Training restarted with the fix: 21 specialists × 500 generations, about two hours.

entries.title: First two specialists: generalist 71%, Witch 84%
entries.html:
The generalist (any kingdom, all 26 cards) climbed from 59% to 71.2% in 500 generations (5 minutes): 79% against Big Money, 71% against Smithy–Big Money, 63% against Witch–Big Money. For comparison, k1-steam scores 43.7% on random kingdoms.

The Witch specialist reached 83.8% on kingdoms with a Witch (97% / 93% / 60% against the three bots). The best old model, k4-20260614, scores 78.9% on its own Witch kingdoms. Nineteen specialists to go.

entries.title: portfolio-v1 released: 79% on random kingdoms, almost twice k1-steam
entries.html:
All 21 specialists finished (500 generations each, about 5 minutes per specialist). They became one model, models/portfolio-v1/, together with the best old model k4-20260614. It is now the default and the selector's first choice.

Test: 200 random Steam kingdoms the model never saw, 40 games per seat against each fitting bot, played the way the autopilot plays today (the nine blocked cards are never bought):

PlayerScore
portfolio-v1 (picks per kingdom)79.3%
best possible pick in hindsight81.9%
best single specialist (remodel, never buying Remodel)75.7%
k4-20260614 (old best)50.9%
k1-steam (every Steam game so far)41.9%

The pick works: it gets within about two and a half points of a perfect choice and beats every single specialist. With all 26 cards allowed the portfolio would score 80.1%, so teaching the autopilot the nine missing cards is worth about one and a half points overall. The Gardens + Workshop specialist is the clearest case: 87.6% in training but 6.9% without Workshop, so it is never picked today. Workshop is the first card to teach the autopilot.

The stored benchmark (policy.bench) is 75.0%: 87% against Big Money, 74% against Smithy–Big Money, 64% against Witch–Big Money.
